claim: Simulated people mediate nearly all transactions
originalWording: Simulated people mediate nearly all transactions

sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)
sources.locator: P02 Business in 2019, simulated-person transactions bullet

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: Simulated AI personas mediate nearly all commercial transactions, often transacting agent-to-agent without direct human involvement.
strict.rationale: Ordinary 2019 checkout and electronic banking did not use AI simulated people, and even in 2026 agentic commerce protocols (announced in late 2025) represent a negligible fraction of real-world transactions.
changedConditions: Enforces the 'nearly all transactions' and simulated-person mediation clauses

evidence.title: Google: Agent Payments Protocol AP2
evidence.note: Protocol and reference implementations; not evidence most real-world transactions use simulated people.

evidence.title: Google Cloud and PayPal: Agentic commerce solution
evidence.note: Commercial offering and agent interaction architecture. No market-wide transaction-share denominator supplied.

evidence.title: US Census: Quarterly retail e-commerce, 2026
evidence.note: Second quarter 2026 e-commerce share 17.1% of retail sales by value. Not B2B, securities trading, or a count of all transactions.

reference.criterion: The vast majority of transactions involve an AI-like simulated person, often agent-to-agent without direct human involvement.
reference.rationale: Ordinary online checkout and payment automation in 2019 were not predominantly simulated-person interactions. Agent payment protocols and commercial conversational-commerce offerings now make the direction concrete. They do not establish the original vast-majority share.

broader.criterion: Commercial AI agent protocols begin enabling software agents to assist with or execute online purchases.
broader.rationale: Google's September 2025 Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) and the October 2025 Google Cloud–PayPal agentic commerce rollout show early commercial infrastructure for agent-mediated transactions. Even charitably, early protocols with negligible transaction volume earn partial credit rather than fulfilling 'nearly all transactions.'
changedConditions: Credits 2025 agentic-commerce infrastructure as partial without equating early protocols to 'nearly all transactions'
